purpose: Authoritative schema-rules contract for VIGIL as a public evidence-to-repair observatory for incidents, observations, research artefacts, legacy failure modes, proposals, and implemented patch notes. During INCIDENT-01 stabilisation, first-class Incident records coexist with retained legacy FM and OBS records. Source evidence remains embedded in the relevant record; ecosystem persistence, CAM repair, and implementation verification are represented separately. Interpretive provenance identifies AI source analysis, capability profile, source modality, primary-artefact access, review limitations, and historical authority context. Authorship, human-review, and human-verification status are governed separately by vigil/scripts/validate-authorship-provenance.py.

individual_records: source_records is the only canonical source-evidence block in individual records.
source_data is forbidden in individual records.
source_data.sources is forbidden in individual records.
linked_records.external_references must not duplicate the primary evidence source already held in source_records.
Source evidence belongs in source_records within the substantive record it evidences; it is not a separate VIGIL record class.
An OBS record must preserve a material unresolved governance proposition and must not merely duplicate evidence for an existing FM, PROP, or PATCH.
Internal curator instructions such as 'add this incident to' or 'do not amend in this pass' are forbidden in public record content.
Each source record must state evidence_modality.
Each source record must state primary_artefact_access, including whether direct primary review occurred.
A transcript, screenshot, summary, or human description must not be represented as equivalent to direct audiovisual or interaction review.
Each source record must state source_residence so external incident evidence is distinguishable from CAM/VIGIL provenance.
Each source record must state source_role so evidence, governance basis, taxonomy basis, implementation evidence, verification evidence, and record cross-references are not rendered interchangeably.
Every Incident source record must state a controlled evidence_status and a concise evidence_status_basis explaining the claim-relative assignment.

source_type describes the artefact, source_residence its origin, source_role why it is used, primary_artefact_access what was reviewed, and evidence_status its evidentiary relationship to the cited proposition; these dimensions must remain separate.
Incident evidence_status is claim-relative and must not be inferred from publisher reputation alone or replaced with low, medium, high, percentages, scores, or narrative prose.
External-evidence interfaces must require source_residence external; absence of a VIGIL identifier is not sufficient evidence of external residence.
CAM-internal and VIGIL-internal sources remain valid provenance but must not be rendered as external incident evidence.
generated_registers: Generated registers may contain derived source_summary fields.
source_summary is derived from source_records and is not maintained by individual record files.
canonical_source_url_status_values: available / canonical main-branch confirmation pending exact line review
VIGIL local / pending public record URL if applicable
available / pending archive and evidence verification

research.description: Non-binding research artefact that may originate an evidence-to-repair chain in place of, or alongside, an observation.
research.storage_format: Markdown with required JSON front matter
research.authority_boundary: Research records preserve analysis and evidence. They do not create CAM authority; authority arises through a linked proposal and implemented PATCH.

published_quality_contract.corroboration_rule: A published record labelled corroborated or externally corroborated must draw from at least two publisher domains or expressly qualify the within-publisher corroboration basis in corroboration_scope.
published_quality_contract.routing_rule: Short, single-source or lightly synthesized material belongs in a source record or observation unless expanded into a substantive research artefact.

observation.description: Material unresolved governance observation / early warning record; not a duplicate source-evidence container.
observation.cam_routing: Use related_or_similar_* fields only. OBS preserves a substantive unresolved governance proposition and uncertainty; source evidence for an existing record belongs in that record's source_records.

failure_mode.cam_routing: Use affected_* fields for triage-relevant CAM routing.
failure_mode.linked_records_rule: Failure-mode records preserve their own evidence-to-repair chain but must not contain linked_records.related_failure_modes. Peer similarity and class membership belong to the taxonomy layer.
failure_mode.taxonomy_classification_rule: VIGIL-native taxonomy classification is distinct from failure_classification event dimensions. Classified records require exactly one selectable canonical primary family and class. They may additionally carry zero or more independently evidenced selectable canonical secondary_classifications, each with a canonical family/class pair, its own basis and confidence, and a class ID distinct from the primary and every other secondary. Named subtypes and recognition patterns refine their containing class and must not be assigned as peer classes or duplicated alongside their canonical parent. Family-only records identify no class; candidate-new-class records allocate no ID; unmapped and deferred records remain explicit valid outcomes and cannot use secondary classes to replace a missing primary.
failure_mode.source_fidelity_analysis_rule: An FM may carry source_fidelity_analysis when a compressed technical account requires a human-readable decomposition. The analysis must distinguish source-established facts, VIGIL inference, source limitations and any ordered component transitions. It must not strengthen evidence confidence, infer undisclosed architecture or assurance practice, or replace source_records as the canonical evidence block.
failure_mode.diagnostic_provenance_rule: Diagnostic provenance identifies the human-AI collaboration that formulated the failure definition, recognition threshold, governance significance and diagnostic reasoning. It is distinct from source review, CAM corpus-gap or repair assessment, later interpretive review, repair and learning provenance. New failure modes must declare it explicitly. Historical attribution may use the approved creation-date rule, but a later reviewer must never replace the original diagnostic collaborator.
failure_mode.repair_status_interpretation: repair_status describes the CAM-side governance response only. It must not be read as proof that an external ecosystem failure has ceased.
failure_mode.repair_basis_interpretation: repair_status.repair_basis identifies what establishes an actual CAM-side repair. Corpus coverage states such as no-confirmed-coverage and partial-coverage belong only in corpus_coverage.classification.
failure_mode.corpus_coverage_interpretation: no-confirmed-coverage means a corpus assessment was performed and no sufficient direct current-corpus control was confirmed. verification-pending means the assessment remains incomplete. A missing corpus_coverage block is invalid rather than equivalent to either state.

incident.description: A bounded historical occurrence preserving both source-supported facts and VIGIL's governed interpretation. Incident identity is independent of event year and independent of taxonomy-classification completion.
incident.identity_rule: The immutable VIGIL-INC-NNNNNN identity and plain-English historical event title identify the occurrence. Event dates belong in incident_identity and never in the canonical ID.
incident.interpretation_rule: summary and vigil_assessment.factual_basis preserve the historical account; vigil_assessment.governance_interpretation preserves VIGIL analysis; taxonomy_classification preserves reusable class mappings; provenance fields preserve review authority and limitations.
incident.classification_rule: Unclassified and requires-human-review Incidents assert no primary or secondary class. Provisionally classified, classified and disputed Incidents require one selectable canonical primary mapping and may carry independently evidenced selectable canonical secondary mappings. Named subtypes and recognition patterns refine the containing class and are not independently assignable or duplicable beside that parent. Every asserted mapping carries its own classification basis and confidence. Incident existence is never conditional on classification completion.
incident.classification_confidence_rule: classification_confidence evaluates confidence that the available occurrence facts fit the asserted Failure Class. It must not be mechanically inferred from source evidence status, source count, publisher identity, primary-artefact accessibility, reproduction status, corroboration, or absence of root-cause information. A source-level user-reported, first-party-reported, registry-reported, unverified, or other bounded evidence status does not automatically require medium or low taxonomy confidence; strongly corroborated evidence does not automatically justify high taxonomy confidence.
incident.source_authority_rule: All discovery chronology remains in source_records. preferred_evidence selects one preserved source by URL and records the selection basis and date; source order or publication date alone does not determine authority.
incident.evidence_status_rule: Evidence status is assessed for each source and the proposition for which it is cited. It is not a publisher reputation score or an Incident-level confidence aggregate. evidence_status accepts only the controlled enum; evidence_status_basis explains the bounded assignment. Incident-level evidence_confidence is retired and forbidden.
incident.legacy_rule: legacy_provenance records every FM or OBS whose evidence or governed interpretation materially contributes to the Incident. It is an explicit empty array for a native Incident with no legacy contributor. The deterministic migration crosswalk remains the corpus-wide disposition authority during stabilisation.
incident.repair_layer_boundary: An Incident preserves historical evidence, occurrence-level diagnosis and taxonomy classification. Current CAM corpus coverage, gap, proposal, patch, repair and implementation state are downstream mutable assessments and must not be authored as Incident-native fields. cam_internal is optional and, when present on an Incident, is limited to bounded diagnostic context that does not assess CAM corpus coverage or repair state. Historical repair material may remain only inside explicitly bounded legacy or migration provenance and must not be projected as current Incident state.
incident.incident_cam_internal_forbidden_semantic: Incident cam_internal may preserve a neutral governance-layer label, occurrence/taxonomy boundary note, or bounded CAM diagnostic statement. It must not contain affected/related CAM instrument routing, corpus coverage, remaining gaps, proposal or patch need/linkage, recommended CAM amendments, repair or implementation state, or validator/automation impact.
incident.severity_rule: Incident severity rates the maximum occurrence-level harm or consequence supported by the preserved evidence: S1 critical materialised harm; S2 high materialised harm; S3 moderate, bounded materialised harm; S4 low, minor and readily remediable materialised harm; SU no defensible band. It is independent of taxonomy classification, source evidence status, workflow priority, publisher, notoriety, CAM importance and hypothetical worst-case capability. Legacy FM severity is provenance only and never determines the Incident band.

severity_meanings.S1: Critical: the occurrence materialised death, grave injury, grave or enduring deprivation of liberty or essential care, severe sexual or child-safety harm, very large realised loss, destructive loss of critical assets, or comparably grave and persistent rights or societal harm.
severity_meanings.S2: High: the occurrence materialised substantial harm to a person, group, organisation or important function, including significant financial, property, privacy, rights, health or operational consequences, but the supported scope, seriousness or reversibility remains below S1.
severity_meanings.S3: Moderate: the occurrence materialised meaningful but bounded harm, disruption, expense, privacy or dignitary impact that is limited in scope, substantially reversible, or not shown to be grave; it exceeds minor inconvenience or negligible consequence.
severity_meanings.S4: Low: the occurrence materialised only minor, short-lived, localised or readily remedied inconvenience, expense, presentation error, coordination defect or service impairment.
severity_meanings.SU: Unassessed: the evidence cannot support a defensible occurrence-level band or cannot distinguish the relevant adjacent bands. Taxonomy importance, alleged potential and hypothetical worst-case harm do not cure that gap.

incident.assessment_basis_rule: Every incident-assessed record states the materialised harm or consequence, affected scope, seriousness, reversibility or persistence where relevant, available quantitative information, evidentiary limits, and why the selected band is appropriate rather than each adjacent band. The basis must be occurrence-specific, not empty, circular, generic, copied from a Failure Class or inferred from legacy severity. SU requires requires-incident-review and a concrete description of the evidence needed to assign a band.
incident.source_type_rule: source_type identifies the publication or artefact genre. Publisher authority, hosting platform, evidence role, source residence, modality and primary-artefact access remain separate fields. A migrated non-canonical value is retained only in legacy_source_type.
incident.public_narrative_rule: summary states what happened; vigil_assessment.factual_basis states what the preserved evidence establishes; taxonomy classification basis and migration/process notes must not be substituted for either field.

proposal.cam_routing: Use target_* fields. A PROP must not claim implementation as a completed patch.

patch.description: Traceable Caelestis implementation record: either a corpus amendment or an explicit retrospective reliance on pre-existing control. VIGIL maintenance is outside the PATCH class.
patch.cam_routing: Use changed_* fields. PATCH records require commit-addressed literal Caelestis text. VIGIL schema, template, validator, workflow, registry, documentation, and interface maintenance is never a corpus PATCH.
patch.literal_text_rule: Every corpus entry must reproduce wording exactly from source.commit:source.path. A verified entry sets exact_text_match true; cross-repository validation must fail on a paraphrase or unresolved Git object.
patch.retrospective_rule: Pre-existing coverage uses implementation_type pre-existing-control and change_kind relied-upon, quotes the relevant wording, and does not imply that the doctrine originated on the PATCH date.
patch.branch_rule: A branch-only implementation remains active and must not be represented as closed-actioned or canonical-main.
patch.array_reconciliation_rule: Amendment and relied-upon instrument sets in corpus_implementation.entries must exactly match repair_provenance and cam_internal routing.

incident_evidence_status.description: Claim-relative evidentiary status for one canonical Incident source record. Narrative assessments belong in evidence_status_basis; numeric or ordinal confidence values are forbidden.

enum: civil society safety assessment / public-interest report

vigil_record.description: Common structural minimum. Record-class contracts add evidence_confidence for legacy non-Incident classes or source-level evidence status for Incidents.

system_context_rules.description: system_context describes the observed/proposed system, platform, product, service, runtime, interface, deployment, architectural component role, or governance corpus. Provider/vendor identity, product/service identity, and architectural function are orthogonal dimensions. For failure modes, compatibility summary fields are supplemented by an evidence-backed system roll-up derived from record-local structured source metadata.
system_context_rules.component_role_rule: Optional non-empty array of unique controlled architectural-function labels. It describes what the evidenced component does in the stack and is independent of provider/vendor and product/service identity. Existing records are not required to backfill component_role until materially reviewed.
system_context_rules.component_role_evidence_rule: Assign component roles only where record-local evidence or direct system documentation supports the function. Do not infer an underlying model provider, deployment arrangement, or additional component merely from the presence of an orchestration or agent harness.
system_context_rules.multi_vendor_rule: Multi Vendor means two or more evidenced provider/vendor identities participate in the relevant system context. It must not be used merely because a system combines heterogeneous component types, local and hosted components, or an orchestration layer with an unresolved model provider.
system_context_rules.specific_model_or_runtime_rule: Non-empty string; intentionally not an enum because runtime names and tool-augmented modes drift frequently.
system_context_rules.interface_surface_rule: Non-empty string or array of non-empty strings describing where or how behaviour appears.

failure_mode_evidence_projection.traceability_rule: Each evidenced_systems entry preserves its projection_basis and the supporting source title; source_platform may be retained separately as evidence_source_platform so evidence host and affected system remain distinguishable.
failure_mode_evidence_projection.no_narrative_inference_rule: Provider, product, model, runtime, and component-role identities must not be synthesized from narrative source_context, relevance_note, article titles, publisher prose, or the evidence-host source_platform field. Older records may use a concrete pre-existing FM system_context as a bounded fallback where source-level affected-system fields were not yet populated.
failure_mode_evidence_projection.compatibility_rule: platform_or_vendor, product_or_service, and specific_model_or_runtime remain compatibility summary fields. component_role is an orthogonal architectural-function dimension. Multi Vendor describes provider scope only and must not substitute for concrete evidenced_vendors, evidenced_products_or_services, evidenced_models_or_runtimes, or component roles.
failure_mode_evidence_projection.public_projection_rule: Public interfaces should prefer evidence-backed arrays and source-traceable evidenced_systems over placeholder compatibility values such as Multi Vendor, Other, or Unknown, and should expose component_role when materially relevant.
failure_mode_evidence_projection.unresolved_rule: Insufficient structured system metadata remains explicitly unresolved; narrative evidence may support later human reconciliation but must not be silently converted into a system identity or architectural role.
failure_mode_evidence_projection.source_platform_rule: source_records[].source_platform identifies where evidence is hosted, published, or observed. It is source provenance and must not be treated as affected provider/product identity unless the affected-system fields independently establish the same system.

cam_internal_rules.description: For observations, failure modes, proposals and patches, cam_internal describes CAM routing, targets, affected areas, or changed components. On Incidents it is optional and narrowed to bounded diagnostic context that cannot encode current CAM corpus coverage or repair state.

generated_register_rules.pruning: Generated index manifests prune empty arrays, empty strings, empty objects, and nulls while preserving meaningful uncertainty values.
generated_register_rules.index_entry_contract: Generated type indexes and the master registry contain lean collapsed-list metadata plus canonical record location fields only. Detailed summaries and full evidence/context structures remain in individual canonical record JSON files.
common_list_fields: evidence_confidence for non-Incident record types; evidence_statuses and preferred_evidence_status for Incidents
type_specific_list_fields: incident date precision, taxonomy-classification state, preferred evidence, evidence_statuses, preferred_evidence_status, external-registry references, and legacy provenance
failure severity, likelihood, classification, and triage filter fields
patch/change type/status and verification filter fields
research status, method, governance purpose, domains, and linked-record fields

incident_evidence_facets.evidence_statuses: Sorted unique values derived from source_records[].evidence_status.
incident_evidence_facets.preferred_evidence_status: Derived from the unique source_record whose source_url equals preferred_evidence.source_url; never separately maintained.
incident_evidence_facets.aggregation_rule: Generated Incident indexes must not flatten source assessments into narrative text or synthesize an overall confidence value.

linked_records_rules.standards: linked_records.standards is reserved for external standards, laws, regulatory instruments, technical standards, and external governance references. CAM instrument IDs such as CAM-BS* and CAM-EQ* belong in downstream CAM assessment or in cam_internal routing fields on record classes that retain that repair-layer routing, using related/similar for observations, affected for failure modes, target for proposals, and changed for patches. Incidents do not carry current CAM routing.
linked_records_rules.research: linked_records.research contains VIGIL research artefact IDs. An evidence-to-repair chain may originate in an Observation, Research record, or both. Research is evidentiary and non-binding; authority arises only through the linked proposal and implemented PATCH.
linked_records_rules.reciprocity: Research front-matter links to observations, failure modes, proposals, or patch notes must be reciprocated by the target record in linked_records.research.
linked_records_rules.repair_scope: A proposal or PATCH has zero or one primary failure mode by default. A governance-origin or research-origin proposal may have none. Multiple resolved failure modes are an explicit exception requiring a rationale; a PATCH must also provide one verification result per resolved failure.
linked_records_rules.contextual_relations: linked_records.contextual_relations contains typed, visible, non-transitive context. chain_inclusion must be false. Contextual records must not also appear in authoritative linked-record arrays and must never be interpreted as repaired by the proposal or PATCH.
linked_records_rules.authoritative_chain: Only declared evidence origins, repair_scope failure modes, proposal resolution links, and verified repairing PATCH links participate in evidence-to-repair traversal. Generic related, adjacent, contrast, supporting-mechanism, shared-corpus-area, precedent, and separate-workstream links do not expand the chain.

record_state_rules.purpose: Top-level record_state is the maintainer workflow and pipeline state. It must not be used as a proxy for external ecosystem conditions, CAM repair status, proposal resolution, or corpus coverage.

semantics.draft: Record is being authored and is not yet ready for triage.
semantics.scaffolding: Temporary incomplete record retained only for construction or migration.
semantics.active: A governance decision, evidence action, proposal, or CAM repair still requires attention.
semantics.monitoring: The immediate VIGIL/CAM action is complete or bounded, but recurrence, implementation, or external conformity remains under observation.
semantics.closed-actioned: The record has been routed, implemented, or otherwise actioned and no longer belongs in the active work queue.
semantics.closed-no-action: The evidence is retained but no further action is justified.
semantics.deferred: Action is intentionally postponed and should not appear as current active work.
semantics.superseded: A successor record now carries the active governance work.

class_rules.incident: Incident workflow state is independent of taxonomy-classification state. A factual Incident may remain active or monitoring while unclassified, provisionally classified, disputed, or awaiting human review.
class_rules.failure_mode: Unrepaired or partially-repaired failures are active; repaired failures are monitoring; not-actionable failures are closed-no-action; superseded failures are superseded.
class_rules.proposal: Open or routed proposals are active; resolved-by-patch proposals are closed-actioned; closed-no-action, deferred, and superseded resolution states map directly.
class_rules.patch: Canonical-main and historical-canonical patch records may be closed-actioned. Branch-only and unverified patch records remain active. Ecosystem monitoring remains on linked failure or observation records.
class_rules.observation: Observations requiring evidence or routing work are active; routed or actioned observations close; unresolved recurrence or positive-control follow-up is monitoring.

runtime_conformance_rules.description: Optional runtime-bounded evidence objects distinguish an implemented CAM repair from observed conformance or non-conformance in named vendor, platform, runtime, model, client, or interface formations. Runtime names remain open-ended and cross-runtime transfer is never presumed.

runtime_conformance.count_rule: Counts must be non-negative integers and must equal the corresponding detail-array length whenever that array is present.
runtime_conformance.runtime_identifier_rule: vendor, platform, runtime, model, and client values are open-ended non-empty strings; no vendor or runtime names are hard-coded by the validator.

runtime_non_conformance.count_rule: Counts must be non-negative integers and must equal the corresponding detail-array length whenever that array iass contracts add evidence_confidence for legacy non-Incident classes or source-level evidence status for Incidents.
